overall_reason: An institutional system used exactly as designed: GDS Transport, GOV.UK blue masthead, plain underlined links, a dated release note, a functional three-way split into Styles / Components / Patterns and copy that names its audience (government service teams) and its job; nothing on the page is decoration.

findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER: 'Community', 'Support', 'Roadmap', 'Principles we follow' are category labels that fit any design system site. The bodies under them are specific ('maintained by a team at the Government Digital Service'), so the cost is only scannability.
findings.after: "Join discussions, events and co-design sessions" (the task the section offers)
findings.why: Category-label heads are the weakest lines on an otherwise task-led page.

findings.evidence: 172 words on one screen (sweep); 'Principles we follow' and 'Community' are two paragraphs each of link-dense prose that would scan faster as short lists of links.
findings.before: Two paragraphs of prose with inline links
findings.after: Keep the first sentence; list the three destinations as links
findings.why: Dense screen in an otherwise well-paced page.

strengths: First screen answers what / for whom / what to do: 'Design your service using GOV.UK styles, components and patterns', for government service teams, 'Get started'.
Dated, specific news ('15 October 2026: We've released GOV.UK Frontend v6.6.0 ... improvements to how the Character count component works').
Owned type (GDS Transport) and colour; the sweep's accent-footprint and 'fake-versions' chrome hits are the brand masthead and a real release number, not slop.
Illustration is a flat diagram of the system's own parts (checkbox, radio, laptop with service page), not stock art.
not_investigated: cookie banner was dismissed by capture prep and is not part of the judgment
